week_quote: Small rituals make ordinary days feel like home.

sections.title: Breathing Wave
sections.tagline: When we move with the rhythm of breath, even stillness feels alive.
body: Sit in a circle. As you inhale, lift your shoulders slightly, as you exhale, let them fall together, like waves in sync.
sections.note: Shoulders up… shoulders down… a very calm rollercoaster.

sections.title: Dancing Movement Chain
sections.tagline: Shared movement builds shared memory.
body: The person wearing something red begins with one dancing movement. Going anticlockwise, each adds their own move. Once everyone’s contributed, repeat the whole chain three times together.
sections.note: If your move feels ridiculous, congratulations, you did it right.

sections.title: A Joyful Flashback
sections.tagline: Laughter is the echo of love.
body: Each person shares one funny or happy family memory that still makes them smile.
sections.note: Pick a memory that still sparkles - like lights you forgot to turn off.

sections.title: Floating Hands
sections.tagline: Invisible connections can be felt, not seen.
body: Hold hands loosely or hover palms close together without touching. Raise your hands as you inhale and lower when you exhale. Feeling shared air between.
sections.note: Let your hands float like they’re whispering hello.

sections.title: Family Orchestra
sections.tagline: Shared leadership makes harmony stronger.
body: Each person picks one sound to sing. Example: la la la, Scoo-be-doo, boom!, hurray! The person whose name starts with a letter closest to letter M becomes the first conductor.
They point to people to start their sound while the second point stops the sound.
Challenge: conductor can use both hands and turn on many sounds at the same time.
Going clockwise, a new conductor takes over but sounds related to each person stay the same.
sections.note: Conduct boldly - even if your orchestra is mildly chaotic.

sections.title: Secret Dreams
sections.tagline: A small invitation to dream as a team.
body: Each person completes the sentance:
‘One thing I’d like us to do together soon is… ‘
sections.note: Dream boldly, even tiny dreams like cocoa refills count.

sections.title: Gentle Stretch
sections.tagline: Joy can live in small movements, especially when shared.
body: Stand in a circle, in silence stretch arms up and out.
Notice how much space your family creates together.
sections.note: Reach softly, no dramatic stretching needed.

sections.title: Follow the Funny Leader
sections.tagline: Imitation becomes collaboration when done with joy.
body: The person with shortest name starts a physical exercise of their choice. Everyone copies for 15 seconds. Go anti-clockwise and switch leadership. At the end, all family members attempt to perform all previous movements in order like a mini-gym
sections.note: Lead with confidence - even if it’s nonsense.

sections.title: One Thing That Makes me Feel Alive
sections.tagline: Energy grows where connection lives.
body: Each person completes the sentence:
I feel most alive when our family…
sections.note: Choose the moment that gives you that tiny inner ‘woohoo!’.

sections.title: Ripple Breath
sections.tagline: Even the smallest breath can touch someone’s heart
body: Sit side by side. As you exhale, imagine your breath sending soft ripples through the air that gently touch everyone else.
sections.note: Exhale like you’re sending a tiny wish across the room.

sections.title: Trust Web
sections.tagline: Trust grows when we move toward the shared goal.
body: Everyone closes their eyes standing near to each other except the oldest person who silently takes a chair and places it somewhere in the room.
The leader gives precise step by step instructions on how the group can reach the chair while keeping their eyes always closed.
Once they approach the chair, the group needs to decide, without speaking and without opening their eyes, the one person who will sit down on it. You can take turns if you like.
When playing with just two people, one is giving instructions and the second person is following them in order to sit on a chair.
sections.note: Move with care - bumping into family members is optional.

sections.title: The Compliment Circle
sections.tagline: Admiration builds warmth and trust.
body: First person turns to the person sitting on their right side and says one word that describes something they admire about this person.
sections.note: One good word = instant sparkle upgrade.

sections.title: Light Between
sections.tagline: When hearts shine together, darkness disappears.
body: Sit together with eyes closed. Breath. Imagine your inner light touching the light of the people beside you forming one shared glow around all of you.
sections.note: Let your glow meet theirs - kindly, not competitively.

sections.title: Shape Switch
sections.tagline: Teamwork forms structure out of chaos.
body: Everyone stands in a circle. The person whose birthday is at summer time or closest to summer calls a simple group shape. Example: everyone makes a circle, a triangle, a straight line, a wave, a star etc.
The family quickly reorganizes their bodies to create the formations together.
Go anticlockwise and next caller continues choosing another shape.
For Two people a Starter calls a shape (circle, triangle, line, wave, star). Both of you quickly form it together using your bodies. Switch roles and keep shaping!
sections.note: Form the shape fast - geometry waits for no one.

sections.title: The Happiness Echo
sections.tagline: Joy multiplies when it travels in rhythm.
body: The first person says one thing that makes them happy at home.
The next repeats it and adds one new thing.
Continue until everyone has spoken.
sections.note: Let your joy echo gently - it’s not Christmas karaoke… yet.

sections.title: Face of Calm
sections.tagline: One minute of releasing hidden tension.
body: Sit close with eyes closed. Relax your faces completely: forehead, eyes, jaw. Together. One collective sigh of peace.
sections.note: Unclench your jaw… yes, that jaw.

sections.title: The Tunnel of Cheers
sections.tagline: Every family deserves a standing ovation.
body: Stand in two lines facing each other, creating a short tunnel. The person with the birthday closest to Christmas starts walking slowly through while everyone claps, hums or chants their name. Continue until all have gone through.
For two people: create a doorway with two chairs, walk through one at a time, the other cheers.
sections.note: If your cheering feels too loud… perfect!

sections.title: Remember When Round
sections.tagline: Shared memories become invisible threads of belonging.
body: Each person shares at least one cozy or funny family moment beginning with:
‘Remember when we…’.
sections.note: Choose a memory that feels warm, like the cookie you weren’t supposed to touch.

sections.title: Joyful Stillness
sections.tagline: Joy is often quiet - like sunlight you can feel, not see.
body: Sit in silence with joined palms. Notice one pleasant sensation and let it spread gently through the whole circle.
sections.note: Look for a warm spark inside - it likes being noticed.

sections.title: Energy Ripple
sections.tagline: Shared energy multiplies when we play with it.
body: Hold hands while standing in a circle. The person whose name starts closest to A begins with one quick squeeze clockwise. Each passes it around. After one full round, person on the right to the Starter begins a second ripple by choosing a new type of squeeze: anticlockwise squeeze, double/triple squeeze, fast/slow squeeze, strong/light squeeze.
The starter needs to get the same kind of squeeze they started with! Challange: different squeezes clockwise and anticlockwise at the same time.
sections.note: Send your squeeze with intention - not like squeezing lemons.

sections.title: Symbol of Love & Gratitude
sections.tagline: Symbols give shape to feelings we can’t always express in words.
body: Together, create one small gesture or symbol that represents your family love or gratitude.
Like placing your hands on your heart or touching fingers together.
Be creative! It should be a unique symbol for your family!
sections.note: Choose a symbol that feels true, even the tiniest gesture can glow like a candle.
